title: Factorized key-role × value-role fast memory
hypothesis: Separate role codes for fast-memory addresses and stored functions can represent useful heldout pairings with less serialized state than an independent matrix per pair, while matching native factor and MAP/Hadamard controls.
physical_object: Associative linear map for each key-role/value-role pair
mirror_coordinate: Pair of discrete key-role and value-role addresses
logical_multiplicity: Compositions of 4 key roles × 4 value roles

development.selection_metric: heldout pair retrieval nRMSE, complete serialized bytes, active MACs

paid_objects: role bases or full pair maps

success_gate: Fresh heldout pair nRMSE <=1e-6, at least 25% fewer bytes than full matrix bank, and no higher MACs than full bank. Mirror-specific value requires beating native role factors and VSA controls.
failure_gate: Quality gate missed, byte reduction <25%, or native role factor/MAP-Hadamard controls match quality with equal/better bytes and compute.
boundaries: Synthetic role composition only; role factors are provided from training-role examples, no learned neural DeltaNet claim.
All 16 pair combinations are enumerated for control payloads; heldout checkerboard pairs are scored separately.
